description: A set of measured numbers with their units, directions and optional bounds. Alone among the six record types it constrains its subjects not at all: a measurements record with no subjects at all is valid, though any evidence anchor then has nothing to resolve against.

body/explanation.label: Explanation
body/explanation.description: Optional in the declared sense only: required for partial and not-applicable, and freely omitted for measured.

body/metrics.label: Metrics
body/metrics.description: Optional in the declared sense only: required non-empty for measured and partial, required empty for not-applicable.

body/metrics/*/value.label: Value
body/metrics/*/value.description: Absence decodes to 0, which is a finite number and therefore acceptable, so this cannot be declared required despite being the point of the record. Nothing re-measures it.

body/metrics/*/unit.label: Unit
body/metrics/*/unit.description: An open set. Nothing constrains which units exist.

go_only_rules.rule: A measured or partial conclusion requires at least one metric; not-applicable requires none.
A partial or not-applicable conclusion requires a non-blank explanation.
A target direction requires a finite target; higher-is-better and lower-is-better forbid one.
A metric's minimum and maximum must be declared together, both finite, with minimum not exceeding maximum.
When bounds are declared, both the value and any target must lie within them.
A metric carries a direction and bounds but no scale, so it is deliberately not the score kind. Declaring it as one would claim a scale that no field carries and no validator checks.
An anchor's subject must name a subject this record declares. With no subjects declared, any evidence anchor is rejected — which is the only thing tying this type's subject set to its body.

The locator kind decides which locator fields must be present and forbids the rest: file-lines and log-lines require a canonical relative path with a positive start and an end at or after it; byte-range requires a path with a nonnegative start and an end strictly after it; json-pointer requires a valid non-root JSON pointer alone; opaque requires a value alone.
Nothing verifies that an anchor points at anything. Anchor content hashes are deferred, so every locator detail is a producer claim.
